standard_prerequisites.name: Coding of trees as sequences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A tree is coded by a sequence whose first component is the number of immediate subtrees, followed by the codes of the immediate subtrees and the root label.
standard_prerequisites.use: SubtreeSeq returns codes of subtrees of the tree coded by t, and the immediate subtrees are read off the code (2210-2218).

standard_prerequisites.name: Primitive recursion
standard_prerequisites.statement: Functions defined from primitive recursive functions by primitive recursion are primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both the auxiliary g_f and the level helper hSubtreeSeq are defined by primitive recursion (2242-2254).

standard_prerequisites.name: Immediate subtrees function
standard_prerequisites.statement: ISubtrees(t) = subseq(t, 1, (t)_0) returns the codes of the immediate subtrees of t and is primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the building block whose sequence-images produce the next level of subtrees (2230-2232).

core_obligations: Observe ISubtrees(t) = subseq(t, 1, (t)_0) is primitive recursive and returns the codes of the immediate subtrees of t (2230-2232).
For a primitive recursive sequence-valued f, show g_f(s, k) = f((s)_0) concatenation ... concatenation f((s)_k) is primitive recursive by primitive recursion on k (2240-2246).
Apply this to h(s) = g_ISubtrees(s, len(s)), the sequence of immediate subtrees of every tree in the sequence s (2248-2249).
Define hSubtreeSeq(t, 0) = <t> and hSubtreeSeq(t, n+1) = hSubtreeSeq(t, n) concatenated with h(hSubtreeSeq(t, n)) by primitive recursion, so level n subtrees are listed (2251-2254).

Bound the height: the maximum distance between root and leaf of the tree coded by t is at most t, so hSubtreeSeq(t, t) lists the codes of all subtrees, and SubtreeSeq(t) = hSubtreeSeq(t, t) is primitive recursive (2256-2261).

proof_roadmap.step: Show sequence-images of a sequence-valued primitive recursive function stay primitive recursive.
Define the level-by-level helper by primitive recursion.
Bound the height by the code and close the construction.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 2219-2224: the function SubtreeSeq(t), returning the code of the sequence of all subtrees of the tree coded by t, is primitive recursive. The author proof (2229-2261) builds it in layers: it quotes the primitive-recursive immediate-subtree function, defines a level-by-level helper hSubtreeSeq by primitive recursion, proves that concatenating the images of a sequence-valued function over a sequence stays primitive recursive via the auxiliary g_f defined by primitive recursion, and bounds the tree height by the code t itself so that hSubtreeSeq(t, t) lists all subtrees. Chaining the two primitive recursions and the closure-of-concatenation argument is genuine construction work.
